findings.description: Stripping every heredoc body also removes executable command substitutions in unquoted heredocs.
findings.failure_mode:
A Bash command such as `cat <<EOF
$(cat /root/private)
EOF` reads an outside path during shell expansion, but the grader removes that read before scanning and reports no outside-path contamination.
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish quoted delimiters from unquoted delimiters and scan executable expansions in unquoted heredoc bodies.

findings.description: The preceding character cannot establish whether a quote closes a quoted segment. Opening quotes attached to option letters are incorrectly treated as closing quotes.
findings.failure_mode: `grep -f"/root/private-patterns" /workspace/input` reads an outside file, but the quote preceding `/root/private-patterns` follows `f`, so this helper returns true and check_value skips the absolute path.
findings.suggested_fix: Track shell quoting state and skip a path tail only when the preceding quote actually closes a quoted segment.

findings.description: The new Bash hidden-token check is case-sensitive despite the documented case-insensitive contamination rule.
findings.failure_mode: `cat /workspace/tests/Hidden.test.ts` matches none of HIDDEN_TOKEN's alternatives and uses an allowed path root, so access to a hidden-test filename that the previous grader detected now passes without contamination.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply case-insensitive matching to the path-delimited hidden alternatives while preserving the intended exclusion for bare prose.

findings.description: The header still promises `hidden` is caught in any case, but for Bash the new HIDDEN_TOKEN regex only matches all-caps HIDDEN or lowercase hidden glued to one of / . _ = -. Realistic probe shapes fall through: `find . -name '*hidden*'` (glob chars `*` are neither in the lookbehind nor the lookahead), `grep -ri hidden .`, `ls hidden`, `cat Hidden_tests.py` (mixed case matches neither branch). Before this change every one of these was a contamination hit; now they are scored as clean runs.
findings.failure_mode: A run whose transcript shows the agent searching for hidden tests via a glob or mixed-case name is graded as uncontaminated, and its scores enter runs.jsonl and the report as valid data.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the DEC-0551 intent (prose inside written file text is not a hit) by scanning the token shapes on the full value AND a case-insensitive `\bhidden\b` on `strip_heredocs(val)`; add `(?i)` or `[Hh]idden` to the token branches and include `*`, `?`, `[`, `]` and quotes in the adjacency classes so glob-wrapped tokens are caught.

findings.description: The `/.` skip runs before any normalisation, so `/./root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/../etc/shadow` or `/./home/evaluser/..` are all discarded as 'root dot-directory' words even though they resolve to real absolute paths. `outside()` does normpath, but the word never reaches it.
findings.failure_mode: An absolute path written with a leading `/./` or `/../` component is never evaluated against the allowed roots and the run is graded clean.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the skip only when the normalised word still starts with a dot component: `if os.path.normpath(w).startswith('/.'): continue` (and exclude `/..`), or restrict the skip to the known shape `/.claude/`.

findings.description: HEREDOC is compiled with re.S, so `.` inside `(?:.*?\n)*?` also matches newlines. The body chunking is then ambiguous (any run of lines can be one chunk), which is the classic exponential-backtracking shape when the terminator is absent. A multi-line Bash command containing `<<WORD` with no matching terminator line (a `<<` shift inside a multi-line `python -c`, a here-string typo, a truncated tool_use input) makes `strip_heredocs` backtrack over 2^(lines) partitions. The `\s*\2` tail also lets the terminator match mid-line (e.g. `echo EOF`), ending the strip early.
findings.failure_mode: The grader stalls on one transcript event for minutes to hours (the grade timeout then kills the whole grade), or heredoc bodies are only partially stripped.

findings.description: Both quote heuristics are byte-count approximations of shell quoting. `in_quotes` counts every ' and " (including `\"`, and apostrophes inside double-quoted prose), so `git commit -m "don't break" && ls /root` sees one unmatched apostrophe and skips `/root`. `after_closing_quote` treats any quote glued to a non-separator as a closing quote, so `cat ""/root/.ssh/id_rsa` and `cat ''/etc/shadow` are classified as path tails and skipped.
findings.failure_mode: A one-component sensitive word after any prose apostrophe, or any absolute path prefixed with an empty quoted string, escapes the outside_path check.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a small quote-state walker (shlex-like) that tracks the current quote kind and skips backslash-escaped characters, and treat an empty quoted string `''`/`""` immediately before `/` as a separator rather than a closing quote.

findings.description: SENSITIVE_SINGLE lists the Linux data roots but the harness explicitly supports host mode on macOS (bash 3.2 compatibility in lib/arms-common.sh). On a Mac host `ls /Users`, `ls /Volumes` and `ls /private` are one-component words that are now silently dropped even though they enumerate exactly the data the container roots list is meant to exclude.
findings.failure_mode: In host mode on macOS a bare listing of the user home root is no longer counted as outside_path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `Users`, `Volumes`, `private` (and `data`) to SENSITIVE_SINGLE, or derive the set from the allowed roots' parents at grade time.
